key_facts: A **halo naevus** is a mole with a symmetrical white ring caused by immune destruction of melanocytes.
Common in children and teenagers (about 1%); often on the back; may be multiple.
Associated with **vitiligo**; the centre may disappear and the ring later repigment.
Reassure if the central naevus is regular; sun-protect the white skin.
Refer a **new halo in an adult over 40** or any atypical centre (melanoma can provoke halos).

sections.title: Overview
blocks: A **halo naevus** is a melanocytic naevus surrounded by a symmetrical **depigmented ring**, caused by immune destruction of the naevus. It is common in children and teenagers and may be multiple.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Cytotoxic T cells recognise naevus melanocytes and destroy them and the surrounding normal melanocytes; there is an **association with vitiligo**.

ul: **"The ring means cancer"**: in young people it is a sign of benign immune clearance.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: The immune system **clears the naevus** and the melanocytes around it.

mech.t: CD8+ T cells recognise antigens on naevus melanocytes.
Naevus cells and surrounding normal melanocytes are destroyed, creating the white halo.
mech.caption: Halo naevus (white ring), blue naevus and Spitz naevus.

mech.t: The central naevus fades and may vanish.
Melanocytes repopulate the ring over months to years in many.

histo: Naevus with a dense lymphocytic infiltrate; loss of melanocytes in the halo.

ul: Central brown naevus with a round or oval white ring; over months the centre fades and may disappear.
The white area later repigments in many.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Clinical with dermoscopy: a regular globular or homogeneous centre with a white halo. An asymmetric or atypical centre, or onset over 40, needs specialist assessment.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: Melanoma with regression or a halo (adults, atypical centre), [vitiligo](condition:hypopigmentation-skin-of-colour), post-inflammatory hypopigmentation.

ul: Reassure if the central naevus is benign and symmetrical.
**Refer an adult (over 40) with a new halo, or any atypical central lesion** (melanoma can provoke halos).
Sun-protect the white ring (it burns easily).
Examine the skin for vitiligo and other atypical naevi.

ladder.t: Dermatology via the suspected cancer pathway; excision for histology.

refer.t: New halo over 40 or atypical centre.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Atypical central lesion or new halo in an adult: **suspected cancer pathway**.
Sunburn of the white ring; association with vitiligo.

pearls: Halo naevi are benign in children; the halo is a sign of immune clearance, not of cancer.

quiz.a: T-cell destruction of the naevus and surrounding melanocytes.

quiz.q: When should a halo naevus be referred?
quiz.a: New halo in an adult over 40, or an atypical central lesion.
